subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Last Monoculture Moments
description: A quick, practical guide to The Last Monoculture Moments.

hook.text: The Super Bowl still draws 100 million live viewers. It's one of the last events everyone watches together.

buildup.text: Series finales once united the nation. Breaking Bad, Game of Thrones, and Succession were rare exceptions.

discovery.text: These events feel special precisely because they're rare. Shared viewing became the exception, not the norm.

twist.text: Even live events are now time-shifted. Many Super Bowl viewers watch highlights on social media the next morning.

climax.text: The monoculture that television created is fading. We now share memes about shows, not the experience itself.

punchline.text: Television built a monoculture, then streaming dissolved it.

quiz.question: Why are events like the Super Bowl considered rare in modern TV?
options: They are too expensive to produce
They are among the last events watched live by a mass audience
